He earned a B.A. from Tarleton State University in 1994 and a J.D. from Texas Tech University School of Law in 1998. He worked for a federally funded legal group in West Texas, moved to Terrell in 2000 to work for two law firms, and in 2003 opened a private practice in Kaufman focused on criminal defense and family law.

notes.text: The court handles misdemeanor and felony cases, CPS and juvenile cases, civil suits, justice court appeals, and a DWI specialty court, according to the county page.

candidates.current_role: Judge, Kaufman County Court at Law No. 2
candidates.background: Bobby Rich is judge of Kaufman County Court at Law No. 2 and presiding officer of the county Bail Bond Board. inForney reported that he spent 21 years with the Dallas Police Department and has worked as a prosecutor, defense attorney and civil attorney. He has lived in Kaufman County for more than 30 years and is a pastor at Gray's Prairie Missionary Baptist Church.

notes.text: He told inForney that his court reviews any case pending more than six months and that the Office of Court Administration reports a 109 percent clearance rate for the court.

q_textualism.summary: Told inForney that judges should "uphold the law as it is written" and that "there is no room for legislating from the bench."

candidates.current_role: Judge, 503rd District Court (Rockwall County), since December 2025
candidates.background: J. Brian Williams was appointed by Governor Greg Abbott in October 2025 to the newly created 503rd Judicial District Court and sworn in on December 1, 2025. He was appointed Rockwall County Court at Law judge in November 2010 and elected to that bench in 2012. Earlier he was chief of the civil division of the Rockwall County Criminal District Attorney's Office, practiced commercial litigation in Dallas, and worked as Rockwall County court administrator and as a legislative aide to Congressman Ralph Hall. He holds a B.A. in government from the University of Texas at Austin (1995) and a J.D. from Southern Methodist University (2000).

notes.text: He was unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary.

candidates.current_role: Rockwall County Criminal District Attorney (first elected 2008)
candidates.background: Kenda Culpepper was elected Rockwall County Criminal District Attorney in November 2008 and re-elected in 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022; the county says she was the first woman to take office as a district attorney in North Texas. notes.text: Her county biography lists her as a vice president of the National District Attorneys Association and a past president of the Texas District and County Attorneys Association board.
